correctness.rationale: Seigal–Sukarto's published primary decomposition gives four fixed rank-two points plus three quadratic components; at \(9\rho^2-14\rho+9=0\), each quadratic has a double root, so the rank-at-most-two scheme has length \(10\) and support \(7\). For a rank-three symmetric Hessian matrix, singularity of its determinant forces \(T(k,k,v)=0\) for every \(v\), hence the kernel point \(k\) is singular on the cubic. The three source-listed cubic nodes yield unique projective kernel-incidence points, exhausting rank-three singularities. The inspected exact symbolic checker verifies all \(3\times3\) minors at the seven rank-drop points, the three corank-one splitting calculations with nonzero fourth-order coefficient, and nondegenerate quadratic germs at the four remaining rank-drop points and three cubic nodes. This gives exactly \(3A_3+7A_1\).
risks: The full \(3\times3\)-minor primary decomposition is a verified literature premise rather than recomputed independently from scratch.
